newsitem.title: USA: Safeway profits up, to open 35 new stores in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Safeway profits up, to open 35 new stores in 1997.

text.p: Safeway Inc., one of the world's largest food retailers, Tuesday reported higher quarterly profits and said it plans about $700 million in capital expenditures and to open 35 new stores in 1997.
The company, which operates 1,050 stores in the United States and Canada, also said it plans to remodel 150 stores next year.

Profits rose to $105.9 million, or 44 cents a share, for the third quarter ended Sept. 7, from $83.7 million, or 35 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales edged up 2.8 percent to $4.0 billion from $3.8 billion.

Same-store sales, including stores that remained open during strikes or lockouts, grew 4.5 percent. This excludes all 86 Safeway stores in British Columbia that were closed during a 40-day labour dispute that ended in mid-July.

Labour disputes in Denver and British Columbia reduced 1996 net income by an estimated 12 cents a share, while a labour dispute in northern California reduced 1995 net income by an estimated 0.25 cent a share, Safeway said.
Operating and administrative expense fell to 22.33 percent of sales in 1996 from 22.94 percent in 1995, it said.

This marks the fourteenth consecutive quarter that Safeway has reduced operating and administrative expense as a percentage of sales. Increased sales combined with efforts to reduce or control expenses continue to lower operating and administrative expense as a percentage of sales.

Safeway said it expects to invest over $600 million for capital expenditures in 1996 and open 30 to 35 new stores and complete more than 125 remodelings. So far this year, the Pleasanton, Calif.-based retailer has invested $324 million in capital expenditures and opened 11 new stores.
Safeway's stock rose 50 cents to $43.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
